# Purpose

This document illustrates how to summarize and visualize a small, **synthetic** set of student marks using base R. It is intended as a documentation example, not an analysis of real students.

## Inputs

The only input is a data frame created in the first chunk. It contains five fictional student IDs and numeric marks out of 100.

## Step 1: Create Synthetic Data

```{r create-data}
students <- data.frame(
  student_id = c("S01", "S02", "S03", "S04", "S05"),
  mark = c(78, 85, 92, 66, 88)
)
students
```

## Step 2: Summarize Marks

The following code calculates the mean, median, minimum, and maximum. Run it yourself and verify the results independently.

```{r summary-statistics}
summary_table <- data.frame(
  statistic = c("Mean", "Median", "Minimum", "Maximum"),
  value = c(
    mean(students$mark),
    median(students$mark),
    min(students$mark),
    max(students$mark)
  )
)
summary_table
```

## Step 3: Visualize Marks

The bar chart compares the fictional students' marks on a consistent 0–100 scale.

```{r marks-chart, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
barplot(
  height = students$mark,
  names.arg = students$student_id,
  main = "Synthetic Student Marks",
  xlab = "Student ID",
  ylab = "Mark (out of 100)",
  ylim = c(0, 100),
  col = "steelblue"
)
```

## Outputs

1. A printed data frame of synthetic marks.
2. A table containing four descriptive statistics.
3. A bar chart comparing marks by fictional student ID.

## Interpretation and Limitations

This example demonstrates a documentation workflow and basic descriptive statistics. The dataset is too small and artificial for conclusions about real educational performance. Check all calculated values before writing a final interpretation.
